record.paper_title: Negative (and Positive) Circles in Signed Graphs: A Problem Collection
record.original_question: Design an efficient method that, given a signed graph Σ, finds a maximum set of pairwise disjoint negative circles or a maximum set of pairwise disjoint positive circles.

evidence.quote: Qn. 2±. Find a maximum set of pairwise disjoint negative, or positive, circles. Ans. Unknown. This is simply a more demanding version of Question 1. An answer should be an efficient algorithm.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A signed graph is a pair Σ = (G, σ) consisting of a finite graph G = (V, E) (loops and multiple edges allowed) together with a sign function σ : E → {+1, −1}. The sign of a circle (a simple closed walk) C in Σ is the product of the signs σ(e) over all edges e ∈ E(C); the circle is called positive if this product is +1 and negative if it is −1. Two circles are called disjoint if they share no vertex (equivalently, in the edge-disjoint version, no edge).

Problem. Provide an algorithm that, given an arbitrary signed graph Σ as input, computes:
(a) a maximum cardinality set of pairwise disjoint negative circles in Σ, and
(b) a maximum cardinality set of pairwise disjoint positive circles in Σ,
and that runs in time polynomial in |V(G)| + |E(G)|. Either exhibit such an algorithm or determine the computational complexity of these two problems.
artifact.status_search_result: The general problem of efficiently finding a maximum set of pairwise disjoint negative (or positive) circles in an arbitrary signed graph appears to remain open. Recent work addresses related and special cases (e.g., packing signatures, antibalanced planar signed graphs of given negative girth, weakly negative circles vs. clustering), but no general polynomial-time algorithm or complexity classification for the problem as stated has been identified.
